, while the data are not yet sufficient to determine the gluons distribution function with a precision comparable to the present precision of the proton distribution function, they are sufficient to determine the triple gluon coupling with a precision comparable or better than the present precision of αs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the triple-gluonic coupling is measured to be g2G/g2S = 1.5 ± 0.3.
the gluon self-coupling can be measured at the Tevatron and the LHC.
the gluon-gluuon coupling is strong, but not too strong.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of pT 4 is feasible in the LHC experiments.
a measurement of the gluon coupling can be made with a precision of 10-15%, provided that one can measure jets or hadrons with transverse momenta of 10-20 GeV.
the pT4 measurement can be used to measure the gluon self coupling, and the result is not sensitive to the details of the gluon distribution.
